gloss: business trip destination; place one is posted to

definitions.gloss: business trip destination; place one is sent to for work
definitions.explanation: The location where someone goes for a business trip. Refers to the destination itself, not the journey.

examples.japanese: {出張先|しゅっちょうさき}から{電話|でんわ}があった。
examples.english: There was a phone call from the business trip location.

examples.japanese: {出張先|しゅっちょうさき}のホテルを{予約|よやく}しておいてください。
examples.english: Please book a hotel at the business trip destination.

examples.japanese: {出張先|しゅっちょうさき}で{現地|げんち}の{取引先|とりひきさき}と{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせをする{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: I plan to have a meeting with the local business partner at my trip destination.

notes:
Compound of {出張|しゅっちょう} (business trip) + {先|さき} (destination; place). The suffix {先|さき} is productive in Japanese and attaches to many activity nouns to indicate the destination or place associated with that activity.

THE ～{先|さき} PATTERN:
- {旅行先|りょこうさき}: travel destination
- {転勤先|てんきんさき}: new post (after transfer)
- {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し{先|さき}: new address (after moving)
- {就職先|しゅうしょくさき}: place of employment
- {連絡先|れんらくさき}: contact information

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出張先|しゅっちょうさき}から{戻|もど}る: to return from a business trip
- {出張先|しゅっちょうさき}で{会議|かいぎ}がある: to have a meeting at the destination
- {出張先|しゅっちょうさき}のホテル: hotel at the business trip location

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {赴任先|ふにんさき}: place of assignment — implies a longer-term posting, not a short trip
- {出向先|しゅっこうさき}: place of secondment — where one is temporarily transferred to work
